title: This, Here, and In a Place

lessons.title: ਇਹ (eh) — this, near here
lessons.gloss: this - the near partner of already-known oh, that

segments.text: Put one familiar contrast back in your voice. Say ਇੱਥੇ (itthe, here), then ਉੱਥੇ (utthe, there). Ask ਕਿੱਥੇ? (kitthe?, where?). Now say ਕਿਤਾਬ (kitāb, book), and the old distant pointer ਉਹ (oh, that).
ਇਹ — eh — this, near here ਉਹ — oh — that, farther away.
You have known ਉਹ from its earlier lesson as he, she, it. That lesson also told you it points to that. Nothing new is being added to ਉਹ now. The new half of the pair is ਇਹ: use eh for a nearby thing.
The same near/far choice already lives in ਇੱਥੇ / ਉੱਥੇ, here / there. Keep the pairs aligned:

utterances: near: ਇਹ (eh) — this. farther away: ਉਹ — that.
near: ਇੱਥੇ — here. farther away: ਉੱਥੇ — there.

segments.text: Wiktionary traces ਇਹ (eh) to Sanskrit eṣa, “this”.
Keep ਹੈ at the end, where Punjabi already taught you to put the verb:
ਇਹ ਕਿਤਾਬ ਹੈ। — eh kitāb hai. — This is a book. ਉਹ ਕਿਤਾਬ ਹੈ। — oh kitāb hai. — That is a book.
Only the first word changes. The book and the verb stay still.

segments.instruction: for a nearby thing, ਇਹ (eh); for a farther thing, ਉਹ
segments.source: [YOU SAY: for a nearby thing, **ਇਹ**; for a farther thing, **ਉਹ**]

segments.instruction: make it distant — ਉਹ ਕਿਤਾਬ ਹੈ
segments.source: [YOU SWITCH: make it distant — **ਉਹ ਕਿਤਾਬ ਹੈ**]

segments.text: Near thing? (ਇਹ, eh.) Farther thing? (ਉਹ, oh.) Near place? (ਇੱਥੇ, itthe.) Farther place? (ਉੱਥੇ, utthe.)
Source: Wiktionary: ਇਹ (eh).

lessons.title: ਵਿੱਚ (vich) — in, at
lessons.gloss: in, at - a place noun first, then this postposition

segments.text: Near and farther: ਇਹ (eh) / ਉਹ. Now bring back two familiar places: ਘਰ (ghar, home) and ਸਕੂਲ (sakūl, school). Ask ਕਿੱਥੇ? (kitthe?, where?).
ਵਿੱਚ — vich — in, at.
English puts in before a place. Punjabi puts ਵਿੱਚ (vich) after it. That is why it is called a postposition: the place comes first.
ਘਰ ਵਿੱਚ — ghar vich — at home, in the house ਸਕੂਲ ਵਿੱਚ — sakūl vich — at school, in the school.
Do not add a verb yet. This step owns only the place chunk: noun, then ਵਿੱਚ (vich).

ਵਿੱਚ (vich) is inherited through Old Punjabi vici and Prakrit vicca from a form reconstructed as Sanskrit vīcya, “middle” (CDIAL 12042). Hindi bīc, “middle”, is a cousin. The old idea of being in the middle became Punjabi's ordinary word for being in a place.

segments.instruction: after ਕਿੱਥੇ?, choose one familiar place chunk
segments.source: [YOU ANSWER: after **ਕਿੱਥੇ?**, choose one familiar place chunk]

segments.instruction: did the place come before ਵਿੱਚ (vich)?
segments.source: [YOU CHECK: did the place come before **ਵਿੱਚ**?]

segments.text: How do you say at home? (ਘਰ ਵਿੱਚ (vich).) At school? (ਸਕੂਲ ਵਿੱਚ (vich).) Which comes first, the place or ਵਿੱਚ (vich)? (The place.)
Sources: Wiktionary: ਵਿੱਚ (vich); CDIAL 12042.

lessons.title: A thing, a place, then ਹੈ
lessons.gloss: the book is at home - a thing, a location, then hai

needs: your eyes or your hands for the steps that ask you to read, point, write or gesture
notice.text: Before we start: this one needs your eyes, so it is not fully a driving lesson. You will want your eyes or your hands for the steps that ask you to read, point, write or gesture. You can listen to everything else now. I will say so again when we reach it, but leave this section until you have stopped: Guided Practice.

segments.text: Say the two pointing pairs: ਇਹ (eh) / ਉਹ and ਇੱਥੇ / ਉੱਥੇ. Ask ਕਿੱਥੇ?. Then say ਘਰ ਵਿੱਚ (vich) and leave ਹੈ waiting; Punjabi keeps its verb for the end.

blocks.title: Grammar Lens: a thing, a place, then ਹੈ

segments.text: ਕਿਤਾਬ ਘਰ ਵਿੱਚ ਹੈ (kitab ghar vich hai)। kitāb ghar vich hai. The book is at home.
The frame has three pieces:
the thing that is present — ਕਿਤਾਬ;
its place — ਘਰ ਵਿੱਚ (vich); and.
ਹੈ at the end.
Punjabi does not need a separate word matching English there in there is. The placed thing plus ਹੈ states that the thing is present in that location.

blocks.title: Grammar Lens: pointing without a postposition

segments.text: When the location itself is here or there, the familiar place word can stand directly before ਹੈ:
ਦੁਕਾਨ ਇੱਥੇ ਹੈ। — dukān itthe hai. — The shop is here. ਦੁਕਾਨ ਉੱਥੇ ਹੈ। — dukān utthe hai. — The shop is there.
The second sentence is the short practical answer this chapter is building: ਦੁਕਾਨ ਉੱਥੇ ਹੈ.

segments.instruction: ਕਿਤਾਬ ਘਰ ਵਿੱਚ ਹੈ (kitab ghar vich hai)।
point near and answer ਦੁਕਾਨ ਇੱਥੇ ਹੈ।
segments.source: [YOU SWITCH: point near and answer **ਦੁਕਾਨ ਇੱਥੇ ਹੈ।**]

segments.text: Ask where the book is and answer that it is at home. Then ask where the shop is and answer that it is there. Keep ਹੈ last.
This is a small curriculum location exchange against a partial inventory. It is not an A1 mock, not A1 readiness, and not evidence of independent human validation.
